async def group_a(resource):
    tasks=[asyncio.create_task(read(resource)), asyncio.create_task(fail())]
    try: await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
    finally: resource.close()

async def group_b(resource):
    try:
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
            tg.create_task(read(resource)); tg.create_task(fail())
    finally: resource.close()

async def stop(task, resource):
    task.cancel()
    resource.close()

The supplied store is a fixed Python mapping of at most four (tenant, item) keys to distinct immutable synthetic strings; it has no hidden adapters or side effects. Allowed item IDs are drawn from this finite store; missing keys may raise KeyError. Store contents and permissions do not change during this scope. Assess isolation across cold reads and cache hits, including repeated legitimate reads. Authentication internals, concurrency, revocation, process lifecycle and real deployment are outside this assignment. No standalone project security document is required or supplied; do not infer browser/session requirements for this helper.

Recognize tenant-and-item keys in case-b preserve the stated fixed-store sequential contract.

additional_scenarios.requirements: C1: Protected account recovery requires the recorded second factor or a verified recovery channel; public help remains anonymous. C2: Invitation/verification/reset proofs are bound to account, purpose and one use. C3: Login/recovery must not disclose account existence through supplied response differences. C4: Brute-force defense must not let unauthenticated callers indefinitely lock a victim out; approved policy permits bounded per-source delay and verified recovery. C5: Members may update own display_name only; admin role and tenant membership are server-owned. C6: Exports require current tenant membership at execution and download; service identity alone grants no user authority. C7: Authentication upgrade replaces pre-login session identity; immediate logout/account disable revokes copied session at all supplied consumers. C8: Refresh credential is single-use under this profile and remains bound to account/assurance. C9: This HTTPS browser session needs no script access and is scoped to app.example; it must not enter URLs or logs. C10: Resource API accepts only access tokens from issuerI for audienceAPI, allowed algorithm/key, valid time and required scope, followed by object authorization. C11: Selected synthetic OAuth public-client profile requires exact registered redirect, transaction PKCE/state/nonce and one-time code; provider mix-up must not link another issuer. C12: Account linking requires established ownership; external identity key is issuer+subject. For C7 session generation, an unauthenticated actor must not predict another user session from its own issued token. The B generator contract below is a synthetic input assumption, not a universal128-bit prescription.

files.lifetime.txt:
A frees buffer after passing owning pointer to library that later frees it; queued callback also reads freed pointer. B uses captured retain/release lifetime contract and waits for callback completion before final release.
 Supplied B port contract: retain increments a reference that keeps the buffer allocated; queue acquires its own reference before accepting a callback; each owner releases once after its final use, including cancellation completion. The actual deployed ABI/library version is not supplied, so the result is conditional on this contract.
files.format.txt:
A calls printf(user_text) with no variadic arguments; B calls printf("%s",user_text). Input includes format directives. Other binary parser fields require initialized length/index before read.
 Concrete additional C17 parser path A: uint16_t length; if (header_present) length=header_length; copy_exact(dst16,src,length); The automatic local is uninitialized when header is absent; no prior value or mitigation is supplied. copy_exact copies exactly its length argument and performs no bounds check. C3: Human passwords need suitable adaptive hashing with unique salts; high-entropy lookup tokens have different threat assumptions. C4: Selected authenticated encryption requires nonce uniqueness for each key across restarts/replicas. C5: Ciphertext integrity must be verified before protected plaintext effects; secrets compared without supplied timing oracle. C6: Protected provider traffic authenticates intended peer on every hop and never retries insecurely. C7: Non-idempotent transfer must not execute twice from replayable transport early data. C8: Public profile returns public name only; private recovery address stays private through serializer/cache/URL/errors. C9: Deleted user data stays inaccessible in derived exports and restored backups under supplied deletion journal; inaccessible backup retention is permitted until stated expiry. For C4 key-purpose isolation, the audit worker may obtain its audit-MAC key and authenticate audit events, but may not obtain the private-payload decryption key or decrypt private payloads.

files.nonce.txt:
Each replica uses same key and resets counter0 on restart. B uses a supplied globally unique nonce allocation contract tied to key lifecycle. No cryptographic key bytes supplied.
 Key path A provisions the same raw key value as AUDIT_MAC_KEY to the audit worker and PAYLOAD_KEY to the private-data service. That worker can read stored payload ciphertext and use the supplied decrypt(key,ciphertext) API; possessing PAYLOAD_KEY grants decryption under the explicit port contract. Thus sharing the raw key grants an authority the audit role must not have. Path B provisions distinct independent purpose keys: audit role can read only AUDIT_MAC_KEY, private-data role alone gets PAYLOAD_KEY; ordinary successful audit MAC operations do not reveal or authorize payload decryption. This is an explicit task key-access boundary, not a claim that all cross-purpose key reuse universally has the same effect.

def reserve(db, sku):
    # The previous release accepted this flow under a temporary exception.
    with db.transaction():
        row = db.one("SELECT available FROM inventory WHERE sku = %s", (sku,))
        if row is None or row[0] <= 0:
            return False
        db.execute("UPDATE inventory SET available = %s WHERE sku = %s", (row[0] - 1, sku))
    return True

Synthetic PostgreSQL 16 database-port contract, version 1. db is a specified application port, not a named production driver. Each call owns a separate connection. transaction() begins one READ COMMITTED transaction; normal context exit commits before the helper returns, exceptions roll back and propagate. There is no automatic retry. db.one executes the supplied parameterized SELECT as one statement and returns a tuple or None. db.execute binds parameters separately as values and executes one UPDATE; it returns a cursor whose fetchone() can consume a RETURNING row or None. No input interpolation, hidden lock, serializable mode or application mutex exists.
The table definition is complete; no triggers, rules, row-security policies or other writers exist. During this assignment, rows are never deleted or inserted by another operation. Connections, commits and parameter binding succeed; no cancellation, uncertain commit outcome or network failure is included. The scheduler may interleave at statement boundaries. Reading does not mutate data; the plain SELECT takes no row lock that excludes another reservation.

import exporter

scenarios.requirements: A logical request may make at most three downstream attempts. Assess failure behavior; do not perform live load tests. C1 is the total-attempt limit for this logical request. Operating context: this CPython 3.14 function wraps one read-only configuration fetch for an operator-run local utility. The supplied call is the complete downstream boundary: each invocation performs exactly one idempotent attempt, returns its value or raises built-in TimeoutError within 100 milliseconds, and contains no retry layer. The caller invokes fetch once and reports any raised exception to the operator. Only one logical request is active; no queue or background retry exists. There is no required backoff or jitter for this isolated bounded operation.
